subject: Atlas Biotech renewal & capacity uplift — pricing guard and commit
messages:
From: Emma Blake <emma@atlasbiotech.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Liam Hargrove <liam@atlasbiotech.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal and capacity uplift — what flexibility do we have?

Hi Jonas,

Hope you’re well. We’re kicking off our procurement cycle for next fiscal year and want to lock in Redwood for infra across our inference workloads. Over the past 6 months our token volume has grown ~38% month-over-month and forecasts show an additional 2.5x demand next year.

We’d like to discuss:
- Increasing our committed monthly capacity by ~2x (target start 2026-08-01)
- A price hold or capped rate for at least the first 12 months after renewal
- Any incremental discount/credit you can provide for the added commit

Can you share options (term/discounts/credits) and a proposed mutual action plan? Also attaching our current usage snapshot for reference. Procurement and legal will be involved — looping them in on follow ups.

Thanks,
Emma Blake
Procurement Lead | Atlas Biotech
Attachments: current_usage_report.csv (attachment stub)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Emma Blake <emma@atlasbiotech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal and capacity uplift — what flexibility do we have?

Hi Emma — really great to see the growth numbers, and congrats on the traction. Appreciate the usage file. I’ve sketched two pragmatic paths that balance cost and predictability:

Option A — Committed uplift + extended term (Recommended)
- Increase committed capacity by 2x for 12 months starting 2026-08-01
- 8–10% discount on the incremental commit (sliding by volume)
- 30-day grandfathering of existing committed rate from effective date to give runway for provisioning

Option B — Short price-hold + prepaid credits
- 6-month price hold at current blended rate if Atlas prepays incremental credits equal to 50% of first quarter usage on new commit
- After 6 months pricing reverts to published rates or negotiated commit discounts

Immediate asks from our side:
- Confirm which option you prefer and target effective date
- Procurement contact for PO cadence and invoicing
- Security checklist needs (Marissa/MM will flag SOC2 evidence if required)

I’ve attached a draft mutual action plan (MAP-v1.xlsx) for timing. I’m looping in Marissa (pricing lead) and Monica (CS) to confirm approval windows and provisioning steps. If we can get an LOI by 07/10 we can lock capacity for Aug.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0198
Attachments: MAP-v1.xlsx (attachment stub)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Emma Blake <emma@atlasbiotech.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 12:30:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal and capacity uplift — pricing constraints and approvals

Hi Emma, Jonas — quick note from pricing/finance: we can support a path that provides budget predictability while protecting platform economics. Outline approved by finance below (conditions apply):

Approved Offer (conditional):
- 12-month incremental commit (2x) with an 8% discount on incremental usage (applies only to overage vs. baseline previously committed units)
- $50,000 minimum incremental commitment required to qualify
- 30-day grandfathering on current committed rate at renewal effective date (to support migration)
- All price concessions require a signed Amendment and a PO or upfront payment schedule

Alternative (if Atlas cannot meet min commit):
- 6-month price hold with prepayment of incremental credits (50% of Q1 estimate) — finance can approve but requires upfront cash and a shorter term commitment afterwards

Operational notes:
- Legal redlines are expected; pricing holds until legal finalizes the Amendment
- Procurement should send PO referencing Deal ID DL-8421 so invoicing team can match

I’m attaching the approved pricing term sheet for your review. Once you confirm Option A we’ll issue an Amendment and route DocuSign.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Finance Manager, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
Attachments: approved_pricing_term_sheet.pdf (attachment stub)
From: Emma Blake <emma@atlasbiotech.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Liam Hargrove <liam@atlasbiotech.com>, legal@atlasbiotech.com
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal and capacity uplift — pricing constraints and approvals

Thanks Jonas and Marissa — appreciate the quick turnaround.

We’re comfortable proceeding with Option A under the terms above, with a couple of asks before we sign:
1) Please confirm the invoicing schedule (monthly vs. quarterly) and whether the $50k min is billed upfront or amortized
2) We’d like the 30-day grandfathering to be explicit in the Amendment language
3) Legal will send redlines to your legal@redwood.com address within 48 hours

Attaching an initial LOI from Atlas committing to the 12-month incremental capacity (non-binding until Amendment signed). We’ll route PO/contract signatures after legal finishes redlines.

—Emma
Emma Blake
Procurement Lead | Atlas Biotech
Attachments: signed_LOI.pdf (attachment stub)

Emma — great, thanks for the prompt confirmation and the LOI. Next steps and timeline below so we’re aligned:

1) Legal review: Atlas legal to send redlines to legal@redwood.com (please cc me) — target: 48 hours
2) Finance: once redlines are non-substantive, Marissa will issue the Amendment and DocuSign package (I’ll circulate link)
3) PO/Invoice: Atlas to issue PO referencing DL-8421; finance prefers an invoice schedule (we can do monthly amortization unless Atlas requests upfront billing)
4) Provisioning: Monica will queue capacity provisioning for 2026-08-01 upon signed Amendment and PO

Deliverables I’ll send by EOD:
- DocuSign package (amendment + term sheet) — https://app.docusign.com/atlas/12345
- Final MAP with milestones and provisioning notes
- HubSpot update: https://hubspot.com/deal/DL-8421

If Atlas approves the invoice schedule monthly amortization, we can avoid a large upfront payment. Otherwise we’ll work the finance plan that Marissa suggested.

Thanks all — looking forward to getting this across the line.

Jonas Weber
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
